answer: A stake-and-work bond works like this: every agent identity must lock a deposit and keep completing verifiable tasks to stay active, so each fake identity costs real money and real compute. Attackers face a summit that grows steeper with every clone they add, because the bond is per identity, not per operator. Looked at through a prism of costs, the scheme makes a thousand sock puppets a thousand times more expensive than one honest agent, and the deposits of caught cheaters are burned, leaving only an umber stain on their reputation record.
